payload.name: Preserve directly-stated facts during extraction
payload.description: When a speaker directly answers a factual question (e.g., how they met, when, where), extract that specific fact as its own memory candidate during extraction instead of only creating a high-level conversation summary.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a direct answer to a factual question (how, when, where, how long), create a separate candidate that captures the specific fact exactly, in addition to any broader conversation summary.
Do not replace an explicit fact with a generic paraphrase (e.g., 'shared experiences about her relationship'); preserve the concrete detail so it remains retrievable later.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction summarized the conversation and lost an explicitly stated fact (how a couple met). The mechanism is over-generalization during candidate extraction, which can drop any directly stated fact. This applies to any session where a speaker directly answers a factual question and that fact must remain retrievable; it does not apply to indirect statements.

payload.name: Preserve_All_Enumerated_Components_In_Extraction
payload.description: When a single message gives advice, strategies, preferences, or facts as multiple distinct items joined by 'and', 'or', commas, or bullets, during extraction preserve every component in the memory content; do not drop any listed element.
content: During extraction, when a single message contains multiple distinct components of advice, strategies, preferences, or facts linked by 'and', 'or', commas, or bullets, preserve every component in the candidate content. Do not collapse the list to one item; check each connector clause and include it explicitly.
Apply the same completeness check when writing or updating memories from such messages: confirm that each enumerated item in the source maps to a distinct phrase in the memory content.

candidates.solves: Extraction dropped the 'set goals' component from a multi-part study tip. The mechanism is incomplete extraction of enumerated components from a single utterance. This rule preserves all explicitly listed components during extraction, transferring to any future construction where advice or preferences are delivered as a list, but not to intentional merges or single-fact messages.

payload.name: Preserve explicit facts during candidate extraction and CRUD
payload.description: When a user message states multiple distinct facts, especially activities plus objects, accessories, or answers to direct questions, use separate extraction candidates and verify none are dropped before UPDATE or MERGE.
content: During extraction, when a single user message states multiple distinct explicit facts, do not consolidate them into one activity-focused summary. Create separate candidates for facts about objects, accessories, clothing, preferences, or answers to direct questions, ensuring every explicit claim appears in at least one candidate.

Before applying an UPDATE, MERGE, or ADD, re-check the candidate against its source messages; if an explicit fact is missing, add it to the candidate or create an additional candidate rather than letting it be dropped.
When a fact does not fit an existing memory's dominant theme, record it as its own ADD candidate instead of omitting it or forcing it into an unrelated enrichment.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction collapsed a multi-fact message into one activity summary, omitting an explicit object/accessory fact that later questions rely on. The reusable failure is incomplete candidate coverage when a message mixes activities with separate objects, preferences, or answers to direct questions. The rule requires every explicit claim to survive in some candidate, using separate ADD candidates when facts do not share the dominant theme. It applies to any future extraction/CRUD session with multi-fact user messages; it does not apply to inferring facts the user never stated.

payload.name: PreserveAllActivityComponents
payload.description: When extracting an activity that covers multiple distinct areas or topics, ensure every area is kept as an equal component in the memory content.
content: During extraction, when a memory subject performs an activity (seminar, class, program, campaign, etc.) covering multiple distinct areas or topics, represent each area as an equal component in the memory content (e.g., 'seminars on X and Y'), not as a modifier of the first area.

Before creating an ADD/UPDATE candidate, scan the source for all explicitly listed areas linked by 'and', 'as well as', or 'plus'; confirm each appears in the candidate's content and object fields; if any is missing, revise the candidate.

candidates.solves: When a source describes one activity spanning multiple distinct areas (e.g., seminars on sports and marketing), extraction may treat the first area as the activity type and demote others, losing a fact. This skill requires storing all listed areas as equal components. It applies to any activity with a conjunctive list in future sessions, and does not apply when only one area is truly named.

payload.name: ExtractAdditionalHobbiesAfterAlso
payload.description: When a user describes a person's hobbies or interests and later adds another with 'also', 'too', or 'and', extract the additional one as a separate durable fact.
content: During extraction, if a user states a hobby/interest for a person and then in a later turn adds another hobby/interest with 'also', 'too', or 'and', create a separate candidate memory for the additional item.
Do not treat the later item as a paraphrase of the earlier statement or skip it because the topic was already captured; each explicitly named hobby or interest is a distinct fact.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops a second hobby or interest when the user adds it in a follow-up turn with 'also' after a previous turn already yielded a memory. The rule forces extraction of each explicitly named attribute separately, preventing incomplete memory profiles. Applies to any conversation where a person's hobbies or interests are enumerated across adjacent turns.

payload.name: Preserve-all-enumerated-hobbies-and-interests
payload.description: When a user explicitly names multiple hobbies, interests, or enjoyed activities in one message, apply during extraction and CRUD to ensure every listed item is stored, not just the first or most elaborated one.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly enumerates a person's hobbies, interests, or enjoyed activities (e.g., 'X and Y' or 'A, B, and C'), preserve every listed item in memory candidates. Do not drop secondary items because they receive less explanation or emphasis.
If the message elaborates on only one item, still capture the other listed items in the same or separate candidates so the complete preference set is stored.

During CRUD, before accepting an ADD, compare the candidate against the source message; if any explicitly listed hobby/interest item is missing, supplement the candidate or update the existing memory instead of committing an incomplete one.

candidates.solves: When extracting memories from a message where a user explicitly lists several hobbies, interests, or enjoyed activities, the constructor may capture only the first or elaborated item and omit the rest, leaving the memory incomplete for later questions. This Skill enforces that all enumerated items in such statements are preserved, avoiding missing preference claims. It applies to any future message with explicit multi-item hobby/interest/enjoyment lists, not to implied or vague statements.

payload.name: Extract-All-Enumerated-Items
payload.description: When a user message contains multiple listed pieces of advice, preferences, facts, or requirements, use during extraction to capture every item instead of only the first few.
content: When extracting candidates from a message that presents several distinct items in a list (numbered, bulleted, or natural-language 'also/and'), include all enumerated items. Combine them into one candidate if they share a subject, or create separate candidates; do not drop trailing items. Before finalizing an extraction candidate, recheck the raw message to confirm every listed item is represented.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: extraction candidate omitted the last piece of advice from an enumerated list, so later ADD only persisted partial information. The abstraction: any extraction step must treat enumerations as complete sets and preserve every listed item. This applies whenever future messages contain multiple distinct advice, preferences, or facts in one utterance; it does not require knowing the gold answer and is not limited to a particular topic.

payload.name: Preserve all explicit feelings in extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly states multiple feelings or attributes about the same activity or subject, include all of them in the extracted memory candidate instead of selecting only one.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source text explicitly lists multiple distinct feelings, preferences, or attributes about the same subject or activity (e.g., 'exciting and free-feeling'), capture every listed element in the memory content. Do not drop any explicit descriptor even if one seems more salient; paraphrase only to combine them concisely.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates often drop one of multiple explicitly stated feelings about the same activity, losing a claim. The rule: when a message lists multiple distinct feelings or attributes, retain all explicit descriptors. This applies to any future extraction where a single subject has several explicit evaluative terms.

payload.name: Preserve all explicitly listed elements in extracted memories
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists two or more distinct topics, activities, preferences, or facts (e.g., joined by 'and' or commas), extract each element separately instead of merging or dropping any.
content: During extraction: if the source statement explicitly enumerates multiple items, topics, activities, preferences, or facts (e.g., 'dreams and life'), include every listed element in the candidate memory content. Do not replace the full list with a single umbrella phrase or omit any item.
When updating existing memories, preserve all previously recorded listed elements unless the new message explicitly changes or removes one.

candidates.solves: Diagnosed cause: candidate extraction paraphrased an explicitly enumerated pair ('dreams and life') into a single theme, dropping one element. The reusable failure mechanism is lossy summarization of explicit lists during memory extraction. This applies to future conversations where a speaker enumerates multiple topics, activities, preferences, or facts in one clause; the extracted memory should retain every listed element so later questions can be answered completely.

payload.name: Preserve all components of stated symbolic meanings
payload.description: When a speaker explains what something symbolizes, stands for, or means and lists multiple aspects, preserve every listed component during extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source text describes what something symbolizes, stands for, or represents and mentions multiple components, keep every explicitly stated component in the candidate content.
Do not replace a specific listed component (activity, context, or purpose) with a broader paraphrase that drops it; include the full set of meanings exactly as stated.

candidates.solves: During construction extraction, candidates may paraphrase a multi-part symbolic meaning and drop one explicitly stated component, leaving memory incomplete and future answers wrong. This skill is a reusable extraction rule: when source text defines what something symbolizes, stands for, or means, preserve all listed components rather than summarizing them away. It applies to any future statement that explains the meaning or representation of an object, phrase, tattoo, logo, or action.

payload.name: Preserve-explicit-general-claims-in-event-memories
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from multiple messages, if the speaker explicitly mentions a general activity or category, include that claim as a distinct fact even when specific examples are also recorded.
content: During extraction, when a speaker describes an experience across multiple turns, include every explicitly stated general activity or category in the memory content, even when you also list specific examples—the general claim is independently queryable.
Re-check all source messages for umbrella terms and quantifiers (e.g., 'many', 'various', 'lots of') and represent them in the candidate; do not collapse the umbrella into its examples.

candidates.solves: The extraction candidate summarized a trip by specific activities but omitted the explicit umbrella claim 'went on many excursions', leaving the memory incomplete for a later query about that general activity. The underlying mechanism is dropping a general, independently queryable claim once its examples are captured. This rule applies to any multi-turn event extraction where a speaker states both a category and instances; preserving the category prevents partial-coverage failures.

payload.name: Extract explicit personal resolve statements
payload.description: When a speaker makes an explicit first-person commitment or refusal about their own future behavior (e.g., 'I won't quit'), extract and store it as a memory.
content: Recognize explicit first-person statements of commitment or refusal about the speaker's own future behavior (e.g., 'I won't quit', 'I'm not giving up') as memory-worthy candidates.
Store such statements as a `state` or `plan` memory tied to the speaker, specifying the action/behavior; do not dismiss them as conversational filler or reassurance.

candidates.solves: The construction stage often misses explicit first-person commitments like 'I won't quit' or 'I'm not giving up' because they are phrased negatively or as reassurance. This Skill ensures such statements are extracted and stored as a state/plan memory. It applies to any message where a speaker directly states their own future resolve or refusal; not to hypotheticals, third-party statements, or general advice.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Role and Trait Attributions
payload.description: When extracting a memory from a message where a speaker explicitly states another person's role or qualities, capture the specific attribution instead of reducing it to generic encouragement.
content: During extraction, if a source message contains an explicit statement about a person's role, title, or qualities (e.g., 'you are a perfect mentor', 'your positivity and determination will make it a hit'), create or update a memory candidate that records that specific claim, including the exact trait words used, and do not replace it with a vague paraphrase such as 'encourages' or 'believes in potential'.

When the same message also contains separate encouragement or support, keep the explicit attribution as its own memory candidate or as an explicit, retained part of the candidate content so the fact remains directly answerable later.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that an extraction candidate paraphrased an explicit role and trait attribution (being a perfect mentor, having positivity and determination) into generic encouragement, making the fact unanswerable later. This rule addresses any future message where a speaker explicitly attributes a role, title, or personal quality to someone; the reusable failure mechanism is replacing specific claims with vague supportive summaries. It applies during candidate extraction in Construction and prevents the loss of answerable facts before CRUD decisions.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Current Focus Statements in Extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly states what someone is currently focusing on, doing lately, or prioritizing, preserve that direct claim as a candidate during extraction and do not let supporting examples replace it during CRUD.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit statement of current focus, priority, or engagement (e.g., 'I've been focusing on X and Y'), create a candidate that records that direct claim even when you also extract concrete examples or activities.
When updating or merging an existing memory with new examples, include both the explicit focus/state claim and the supporting details; do not let the examples substitute for the direct statement.
If the existing memory covers related activities but lacks the explicitly stated current focus, add the focus statement through UPDATE or MERGE rather than only appending the activities.

candidates.solves: Construction candidates often keep the concrete examples from a message but drop the speaker's explicit statement of current focus or priorities. This failure occurred when 'focusing on studying and my relationship' was reduced to only the beach-trip example, so the stored memory lacked the directly stated focus. Future messages that explicitly name what someone is focusing on, doing lately, or prioritizing need the direct state claim preserved alongside any supporting activities.

payload.name: Extract_commitments_as_plan_memories
payload.description: When a speaker promises, offers, or agrees to perform a future action for another person, extract a plan memory even if the action has not yet happened.
content: During extraction, if a speaker promises, offers, or agrees to carry out a future action for another person (e.g., send, write, mail, bring, call, help), extract a candidate plan memory capturing the action, recipient, and topic/object, regardless of whether the action has occurred yet.
During CRUD, when such a commitment appears in the session or retrieved memories, create or update a plan memory; do not dismiss polite offers or future-tense statements as non-memorable.

candidates.solves: Construction pipelines often drop explicit commitments or offers to perform future actions, treating them as non-factual or merely polite statements. This leaves later questions about how something will be done unanswered. The rule applies to any speaker promise/offer/agreement to do a future action for someone else, across topics, and is bounded to action commitments rather than opinions or already-completed events.

payload.name: Capture explicit offers of help or tips
payload.description: During extraction, when a participant explicitly offers assistance, tips, support, or future help to another participant, create a memory recording the offer and its topic.
content: If a message contains an explicit offer by one participant to provide help, tips, support, or future assistance to another, extract a memory capturing that offer.
Record the offering participant, recipient, topic, and the nature of the offer (e.g., support or tips) as an event or relationship memory.
Do not require a completed past action; a stated willingness or availability is sufficient.
Ensure the offer is supported by the message wording and avoid adding details not present.

candidates.solves: Construction pipelines often skip explicit offers of assistance, tips, or future help because the utterance is phrased as a conditional offer rather than a factual statement or preference. This causes missing memories about support commitments. The rule applies whenever extraction processes dialogue where one participant explicitly offers help, tips, or support on a topic to another participant.

payload.name: Extract plans and advice as memory candidates
payload.description: When a conversation contains explicit future intentions, planned actions, or advice/recommendations about what someone should do, extract them as memory candidates before CRUD.
content: During candidate extraction, identify utterances where a speaker states an intention to do something in the future or where one speaker recommends a course of action to another; create a candidate for each such plan or suggestion.

For a stated intention, create a plan candidate capturing the actor and the intended action; for advice or a recommendation, create a relationship or plan candidate capturing the advisor, the advised person, and the recommended action.
Do not drop these candidates merely because the action is described as a future possibility or because the speaker uses tentative language such as 'I will', 'probably', or 'should'.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction can skip memory candidates when speakers state future intentions or give advice about those intentions, leaving no durable trace of plans or suggestions. This rule ensures extraction captures such statements as plan/state/relationship candidates whenever a speaker commits to a future action or another speaker recommends one.

payload.name: Extract-explicit-advice-memories
payload.description: When a speaker in the conversation explicitly gives advice, guidance, or a recommendation to another speaker, use this skill during extraction to create a candidate memory for the advice and its recipient/topic.
content: During candidate extraction, identify turns where one participant explicitly advises, recommends, or guides another participant.
Create a candidate memory capturing the advice content, the speaker, the recipient, and the subject/topic, even if the advice is embedded in conversational dialogue.

candidates.solves: The construction agent occasionally omits explicit advice given in conversation, causing facts to be missing from memory. This skill targets the extraction stage to recognize advice-giving turns and generate a candidate memory, preventing such omissions. It applies to any future dialogue where one person gives advice to another.

payload.name: ExtractDirectActionSuggestions
payload.description: When one speaker directly suggests a concrete action for another person, create a memory candidate during extraction; do not skip brief or casual advice.
content: During extraction, generate a candidate whenever a speaker directly tells another person to perform a concrete action, even if the message is short or informal; record the suggested action, the target person, and the speaker.
During CRUD, ADD the suggestion as a compact event or plan memory linked to the source message and timestamp; do not invent details beyond the visible text.

candidates.solves: Construction pipelines sometimes skip direct suggestions when the message is brief or phrased as casual advice. The diagnosed failure was that no candidate was generated for a speaker recommending a concrete action to another person. This rule abstracts that mechanism because suggestions recur across topics and should be stored regardless of surface content. It applies to future sessions where one interlocutor directly advises another to take a concrete action, ensuring the fact is available for later questions. It does not apply to unstated intentions or general praise.

payload.name: Preserve explicit assurance phrases when summarizing endorsements
payload.description: When extracting a memory about someone recommending or promoting a place/experience, include direct positive assurance phrases such as 'you won't regret it' or 'you'll love it' instead of paraphrasing only descriptive details.
content: During extraction, when a speaker is recommending or enticing someone about a place, activity, or experience, capture explicit assurance/evaluative phrases (e.g., 'you won't regret it', 'it's a must-visit', 'you'll never forget it') in the memory candidate, not only descriptive attributes.
When the source message contains both descriptive praise and a direct promise/guarantee about the listener's future satisfaction, preserve both; do not summarize away the emphatic reassurance.

During CRUD, when an existing memory summarizes a recommendation but lacks an explicit assurance phrase present in the source message, issue an UPDATE/MERGE to add that missing claim rather than treating the memory as complete.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed failure was extraction omitting an explicit 'you won't regret it' assurance from a recommendation, leaving the stored memory missing a key claim. This skill addresses the general mechanism of under-capturing emphatic evaluative statements in recommendation summaries. It applies whenever a future session summarizes what someone said while promoting a place, product, or experience.
